new_statements.quote: Además de los fonemas segmentales se dan dos fonemas tonales: alto y bajo. El primero se representa por medio de la tilde (V́); el segundo, por medio de la ausencia de este símbolo.
new_statements.translation: In addition to the segmental phonemes there are two tonal phonemes: high and low. The first is represented by the acute accent (V́); the second, by the absence of this symbol.
new_statements.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo. 1986. Textos bilingües de cuatro narraciones tradicionales borucas. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 12(1): 79-101.
new_statements.locator: p. 82, §3 (note on the phonological orthography, immediately after the consonant and vowel charts; PDF page 4)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (24 pp., scanned; the PDF's metadata). Journal page 82 = PDF page 4; the passage stands at the top of the left column, immediately after the consonant/vowel charts of section 3.4 'Transcripción de los textos' (p. 81) and before section 4 'Textos bilingües'. Rendered the page (page render, 150 dpi) and read the image: printed text is exactly 'Además de los fonemas segmentales se dan dos fonemas tonales: alto y bajo. El primero se representa por medio de la tilde (V́); el segundo, por medio de la ausencia de este símbolo.' -- the acute over V is visible in the scan (the extracted text layer drops it, showing '(V)'), so the reader's quote matches verbatim. The note is Constenla's own or…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Boruca is described as a two-tone language (high vs. low, high marked with an acute accent in the practical orthography); no opened source says anything about word stress or its placement. Corroborated independently by Quesada 2000: 73 ('Boruca has two tones (high, orthographically represented as / over a vowel, and low, unmarked)') with the minimal pair kup 'seed' vs kúp 'egg' (p. 76), and by Elías-Ulloa 2019: 196 ('En lenguas tonales, como el boruca, la tonía ha sido fonologizada').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Elías-Ulloa 2019: 207 notes that phrase-final breathy voice may mark phrase ends and that Boruca intonation patterns remain to be studied.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone (minimal pairs on monosyllables); the statement is a phonological/orthographic note prefacing transcribed texts, not a stress analysis. Data come from the last fluent speakers (Paulina Leiva Morales, 1986; Ernesto González, 2000).
new_statements.identity_note: Boruca = Brunca/Brunka (boru1252, ISO brn), single variety spoken at Boruca and Rey Curré, Puntarenas, Costa Rica; now dormant (no fluent speakers; Elías-Ulloa 2019 fn. 2). All statements refer to this one variety as recorded from its last fluent speakers; no dialect issue.
